sections.figure_alt: A feedback loop with reference and disturbance inputs.
sections.body_md:
The sensitivity function \(S(s)\) tells how much of a disturbance appears at the output. For unity feedback, \(S = 1/(1+L)\). When the loop gain \(L\) is large, \(S\) is small and disturbances are attenuated. The complementary sensitivity \(T = L/(1+L)\) tells how well the output tracks the reference.

These two functions satisfy \(S + T = 1\). This constraint means you cannot make both small at the same frequency. At low frequencies you want \(T \approx 1\) and \(S \approx 0\). At high frequencies you want \(S \approx 1\) (inevitable) and \(T \approx 0\) (to reject noise).

sections.heading: Key equations
sections.body_md:
For unity feedback:
\[
S(s) = \frac{1}{1 + L(s)}, \quad T(s) = \frac{L(s)}{1 + L(s)}, \quad S + T = 1.
\]

The transfer from disturbance \(d\) at the output to output is \(S\). The transfer from reference \(r\) to output is \(T\). The transfer from reference to error is \(S\).

Peak sensitivity \(M_s = \max_\omega |S(j\omega)|\) is a robustness measure. The reciprocal \(1/M_s\) is the closest approach of the Nyquist curve to \(-1\).

sections.heading: Worked example
sections.body_md: A loop has \(L(j\omega) = 10\) at \(\omega = 0.1\) rad/s. The sensitivity is \(S = 1/11 = 0.091\). A disturbance of amplitude 5 at the output is reduced to \(0.091 \times 5 = 0.45\) at the output after the loop responds. The complementary sensitivity is \(T = 10/11 = 0.91\), so a reference of 10 gives output \(0.91 \times 10 = 9.1\). The tracking error is \(10 - 9.1 = 0.9 = S \times 10\).

sections.heading: Common pitfalls
sections.body_md: The identity \(S + T = 1\) holds for unity feedback. With a sensor dynamics \(H \ne 1\), the output sees \(G/(1+GH)\), which is not \(T = L/(1+L)\). Confusing \(S\) and \(T\) swaps disturbance rejection and tracking. A small \(|S|\) does not mean the system is insensitive to everything; it means disturbances at the output are attenuated.

sections.heading: Where this leads
sections.body_md: The Gang of Four (\(S\), \(T\), \(PS\), \(CS\)) fully characterizes a loop. Robust stability bounds \(|T \cdot \Delta| < 1\) for multiplicative uncertainty. Robust performance bounds combine \(S\) and \(T\) with uncertainty models. The waterbed effect and Bode integrals show fundamental limits on \(S\).
